bullets.title: TSMC Raises Chip Prices 5-10% for 2027; Semiconductor Rally Broadens
bullets.body: TSMC plans to raise prices 5-10% on advanced and mature nodes starting January 2027, with up to 15% premium for high-volume HPC orders. Negotiations concluded in July. The announcement sparked a broad semiconductor rally: SOXX +4.5%, INTC +5.9%, MU +6.3%, MRVL +5.7%, ARM +5.1%, memory names including Kioxia +17%. Record iShares SOXX inflows of $6.13B MTD.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley Software Sweep: Downgrades ADBE, CRM, INTU, WDAY; Upgrades MSFT, PANW, CRWD
bullets.body: Analyst Adam Wood assumes coverage across software with a sweeping ratings reset. ADBE cut to Underweight ($240 PT from $365), WDAY to Underweight ($145 PT), CRM and INTU to Equal-weight. MSFT assumed Overweight with $600 PT (49% upside); PANW raised to Top Pick at $387, CRWD to $227. Framework distinguishes 'moat' (durability) from 'journey' (AI growth trajectory); infrastructure and cyber benefit now, application software later.

bullets.title: US-Iran War Escalates: Strait of Hormuz Shut, Brent Spikes Toward $90; Oil at Multi-Year Supply Lows
bullets.body: US-Iran conflict entered its 10th consecutive day of strikes; tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz, no commercial vessels transited in a 24-hour window. Goldman Sachs warns Brent could reach $120/bbl if closure persists. US SPR at a 43-year low. Brent settled at $89.22/bbl (+1.27%) Monday. Polymarket pricing 65% probability of US announcing ceasefire by August 31.

bullets.title: Futures Bounce: NDX +140bps Pre-Market on AI Trade Recovery; SOX Momentum Unwind ~75% Complete
bullets.body: Nasdaq futures up 140bps Tuesday morning with S&P +0.4%; Asia markets led by Taiwan (+3.1% to record), KOSPI +4.35%, Nikkei +3%. JPM estimates the Korean leveraged ETF unwind is ~75% complete and momentum factor drawdown (~13%) is within typical 10-15% unwind range. Tech ETF inflows led at $6.6B (3.1z) with $4.2B into SOXX semis Monday.

bullets.title: New US Tariff Wave: 50% on Canadian Goods Effective Aug 19; Section 301 on Dozens of Nations Imminent
bullets.body: Trump administration invoking Section 338 to impose 50% tariffs on select Canadian imports (wine, hockey sticks, dairy, wood products; energy/potash/critical minerals exempt) effective August 19. Separately, Section 301 tariffs on dozens of countries expected as soon as this week, replacing 10% global duties with 10-12.5% rates.

bullets.title: China AI Export Controls Tightening; Commerce Discusses Restricting Model Weight Downloads and Training Data Transfers
bullets.body: China's Ministry of Commerce held talks with Alibaba, ByteDance, and Zhipu AI on potential restrictions on overseas transfer of AI model weights and key training data. Separately, broader semiconductor export controls under review. Chinese token share on OpenRouter hit a record ~58% weekly, driven by Kimi K3 and Alibaba Qwen3.8 Max.

bullets.title: NVDA Discloses 9.3% Passive Stake in Nebius; Semis Account for ~Half of Q2 S&P Earnings Growth
bullets.body: NVIDIA filed 13G showing a 9.3% beneficial stake in Nebius (NBIS) comprising 1.19M shares plus ~21M shares via a $2B prefunded warrant. Separately, semiconductors are expected to account for nearly half of S&P 500 Q2 earnings growth, and the S&P EPS guidance ratio hit 1.4x (above/below), near the strongest since 2021.

bullets.title: Big Tech Earnings Slate: GOOGL, TSLA Wed; INTC, TXN, NOW Thu — Hyperscaler Capex as Key Swing Factor
bullets.body: GOOGL (Weds AMC, $2.88 EPS/$117B rev) and TSLA kick off Mag-7 season. Street focused on Alphabet's cloud growth, AI capex ROI, Gemini capacity, and the Frozen v2 chip timeline. Tesla focus on robotaxi scale and Optimus production (limited through FY27). Mag-7 expected to post 31.1% y/y Q2 EPS growth vs 22.8% for the S&P 493.

bullets.title: Oracle Default Risk at Multi-Year High; May Need $7B+ Collateral for Wisconsin Data Center
bullets.body: Oracle's credit default risk protection hit a multi-year high as the market questions AI investment payoff; the company may need to post over $7B in collateral for a Wisconsin data center under stricter power-regulator credit rules. AI-related debt issuance industry-wide hit $489B YTD 2026 vs $322B full-year 2025, with 40% from non-hyperscalers.

bullets.title: UBS Launches Bull Case on US Equities: S&P 8100 by Year-End, 8900 in 18 Months on 25% EPS Growth
bullets.body: UBS Keith Parker targets $350 EPS 2026 and $410 in 2027 (25% EPS growth over 18 months), with S&P at 8100 by year-end and 8900 in 18 months. Market seen as cheap vs. framework: PEG ratios on forward sales growth near post-GFC lows; tech to represent 50% of earnings next year. Overweights tech/semis, financials, healthcare; underweights retail/staples.

bullets.title: Jefferies: Hyperscaler AI Capex Return Risk Rising; Top 5 US Firms Carry $662B Off-Balance-Sheet DC Commitments
bullets.body: Jefferies strategist Chris Wood flags growing risk that hyperscalers may suddenly question AI capex ROI, triggering funding pullback. Top 5 US hyperscalers have accumulated $662B in future data center lease commitments off-balance-sheet, with circular vendor financing arrangements adding systemic risk. Long-term base case: massive capital destruction in US as cheaper open-sourced Chinese LLMs capture share.

bullets.title: China State Support: Record $2B Into Semiconductor ETF; KOSPI Dip-Buying as Leveraged Unwind Nears End
bullets.body: China's government injected a record CNY13.8B ($2B) into China's largest semiconductor-tracking ETF on Monday, signaling policy backing. Korea KOSPI down 28% from June peak but fundamentals remain solid; JPM maintains OW with 12,500 KOSPI 12-month target. Korea logged record ETF inflows with leveraged ETF unwind estimated ~75% complete.

bullets.title: Fed in Blackout Period; Only 15% Probability of July Cut; September 50/50
bullets.body: The Fed enters its blackout period ahead of the July 29 FOMC decision with only a 15% implied probability of a July cut. September rate hike probability is near 50/50 despite cooler June inflation prints. Fed Chair Warsh task forces focused on: less forward guidance, QE review, AI as disinflationary force, and money supply focus.

bullets.title: Ackman/Pershing Square Rotation: MSFT Over GOOGL; Leverage Cited as Top Market Risk
bullets.body: Pershing Square reduced Alphabet by 95% and initiated 5.7M MSFT shares. Ackman constructive on equities overall, favoring durable AI-beneficiary compounders (MSFT, AMZN, META, UBER, Brookfield). Calls excessive leverage 'greatest market risk' that could trigger forced selling in a macro shock.

bullets.title: ECB Bank Lending Survey: Eurozone Banks Tighten in Q2; Wage Growth Expectations Ease to 2.5%
bullets.body: Eurozone banks tightened credit standards in Q2 driven by geopolitical and energy price concerns, with SMEs and energy-intensive firms hardest hit. Mortgage demand fell sharply and banks expect further housing loan demand decline in Q3. Wage growth expectations eased materially to ~2.5% from 3.1%, reflecting demand concerns.

bullets.title: Memory Cycle Turning: DRAM Prices Surging in Korea; NAND Shortage to Ease in 2027; BofA Adds MU to US 1 List
bullets.body: South Korean DRAM unit prices are surging in July with accelerating momentum. TrendForce projects the NAND supply shortage to ease in 2027 as server demand hits >40% of total NAND. Xiaomi raised its 2026 smartphone shipment target to 110M units citing a memory market turnaround. BofA added MU to its US 1 List.

bullets.title: UK Data: Employment Strong (+148K vs 80K Est), Borrowing Better Than Expected; New Chancellor Healey Appointed
bullets.body: UK employment change of +148K in May beat the 80K consensus, though average earnings slipped to 4.3% from 4.4%. Public sector net borrowing came in at £16B vs £17.8B estimate. New Chancellor John Healey announced a 5% electricity VAT cut, a modest fiscal easing measure costing ~£850M.

bullets.title: AI Debt Issuance Hits $489B YTD 2026, 52% More Than Full-Year 2025; Hedge Fund Gross Leverage at All-Time High
bullets.body: AI-related debt issuance reached $489B YTD 2026 vs $322B for full-year 2025, with 40% from non-hyperscalers. Separately, total margin debt hit $1.5T and hedge fund gross leverage reached an all-time high — key macro fragility signals cited by multiple sell-side desks.

bullets.title: Intel Announces Fresh Data Center Layoffs Despite 22% Q1 Revenue Growth
bullets.body: Intel is targeting a new round of layoffs in its Data Center and AI Group as part of a broader strategy to become more focused and efficient. The move follows 22% Q1 revenue growth in the segment, suggesting restructuring is organizational rather than demand-driven.

bullets.title: Gold Near $4,080/oz; Silver +3%; Safe-Haven Demand Elevated on Middle East Conflict
bullets.body: Spot gold advanced nearly 2% to $4,080/oz and silver rose ~3% to $58.09/oz as US-Iran military exchanges intensified. Gold is holding near $4,000 as traders balance geopolitical escalation against Fed rate hike expectations and oil-driven inflation risks.
